title: Sable and the Provision
premise: Ulyana Dravenmoor, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries, takes one last contract escorting a government survey team into the flooded lowlands of the Sable River basin. When the team vanishes overnight — gear intact, no tracks, no bodies — Ulyana is stranded in monsoon country with a leaking boat and a stranger named Ivo Kestrel who claims to be a cartographer but knows too much about what took them. As the waters rise and the truth surfaces — the survey was mapping something the government wants buried, and the team found it — Ulyana must choose between fleeing to safety and going back for the one survivor. The story ends with Ulyana burning her blacklist papers on the riverbank: she stops running, not because it's safe, but because belonging finally costs less than survival.
about_author: C. M. Crane is the pen name of a former river expedition cook who spent six seasons in remote basins before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose pasts travel lighter than their gear.

chapters.title: The Weight of Moving On
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In a border town that won't have her, Ulyana accepts a survey escort contract from a nervous bureaucrat — the only work left to someone blacklisted twice. She packs light out of habit, leaving behind a photograph she can't explain keeping. Emotional beat: restless resignation, the ache of permanent transit.

chapters.title: Downriver Contract
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She meets the survey team: five officials, too much equipment, and a leader, Halvard, who lies badly about their purpose. The boat is old; the monsoon forecast is worse. Emotional beat: professional suspicion sharpening into unease as Ulyana reads the river better than they read her.

chapters.title: Water That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. First days on the Sable: drowned villages, marker posts from an older, erased mapping expedition. Halvard grows secretive at night. Ulyana recognizes the route from a job that got her blacklisted the first time. Emotional beat: dread of returning to a place that already cost her everything.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A lone man in a canvas skiff intercepts them at a confluence, claiming to be a cartographer charting flood lines. He knows the river's false channels intimately — and watches Halvard too carefully. Emotional beat: charm layered over calculation; the reader senses Ivo chose this meeting.

chapters.title: Gear and No Tracks
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Dawn: the camp is empty. Five bedrolls cold, boots gone, weapons left, no tracks in the mud that should hold them. Only Halvard's journal, pages soaked but legible. Emotional beat: cold horror — Ulyana has seen disappearances before, never one this clean.

chapters.title: What the Journal Admits
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, intercut with journal entries. The survey wasn't mapping floods; it was confirming that something beneath the basin — a sealed site from a prior regime — had surfaced after the last deluge. The team was ordered to find it and report nothing. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Leaking Boat, Rising Water
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Ivo's alternating POV. The hull starts taking water; the monsoon arrives early. Forced together on repairs, they trade half-truths — Ulyana about her blacklisting, Ivo about nothing at all. Emotional beat: grudging interdependence between two people built to travel alone.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on Charts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They shelter in a stilt village absent from every map, where elders speak of 'the provision' — supplies left by the old expedition, meant for whoever survived long enough to need them. Emotional beat: first warmth of the journey; a community that asks no names.

chapters.title: Ivo's Second Map
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Caught drawing at night, Ivo reveals a private map marking the vanished team's likely path — and his own reason for coming: his sister was on the earlier, erased expedition. Emotional beat: vulnerability offered as currency; trust tentatively extended.

chapters.title: Patrol Lights on the Water
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A government patrol sweeps the basin, hunting witnesses. Ulyana recognizes the officer leading it — the man who signed her second blacklist. They hide among drowned trees while searchlights pass. Emotional beat: terror braided with old rage; running versus standing ground.

chapters.title: The Provision Cache
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Ivo's POV. Following the journal's cipher, they find the provision: a cache of records, rations, and evidence the old expedition hid against exactly this erasure. Among it, a photo — Ivo's sister, alive in the last frame. Emotional beat: grief and hope colliding.

chapters.title: One Survivor
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A radio fragment: one survey member, Tamsin, is alive, held at the patrol's forward post — bait to draw out whoever took the journal. Ulyana could still take the safe channel south. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; she starts paddling toward the trap.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Blacklister
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana walks into the patrol post under a flag of parley, offering the journal's location for Tamsin. The officer offers instead a clean record — for silence about the site. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare; the life she lost, priced against a stranger's.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She refuses; the deal sours into captivity. But Ivo has shadowed her, and cuts the post's boats loose in the night, forcing chaos. They escape upriver with Tamsin, half-drowned. Emotional beat: fierce, costly loyalty — the first time Ulyana chooses people over exit.

chapters.title: Monsoon at Full Voice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The storm peaks. Tamsin, shell-shocked, recounts what took the others: not violence — recruitment. The officers were taken to the site and chose to stay, seduced by what it promised. Emotional beat: horror reframed; the enemy is longing, not malice.

chapters.title: The Site Beneath the Basin
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They reach the surfaced site: a vault of the old regime holding archives of everyone it disappeared — including proof that would clear Ulyana and name Ivo's sister's fate. The missing survey team stands guard over it, unrepentant. Emotional beat: awe curdling into confrontation.

chapters.title: Halvard's Choice
chapters.summary: Halvard's POV. Halvard explains why he stayed: the archive holds his own erased family, and leaving means letting it drown again. He begs Ulyana to understand. Emotional beat: tragic symmetry — he stopped moving for the same reason she always couldn't.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The patrol arrives to seal the site permanently. In the flooding vault, Ulyana must choose: save the archives or save Halvard, who stays by choice until the water forces his hand. Emotional beat: climax — the price of survival paid in full view.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The escape downriver through the storm's worst hours: leaking boat, three survivors, the archive reduced to what they could carry — enough. Halvard drowns saving the last case. Emotional beat: exhausted, grieving triumph; the river exacts its fee.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the capital, the carried records force an inquiry. Ulyana testifies — not for vindication but so the disappeared get names again. Her blacklists are struck; the officer is relieved of command. Emotional beat: quiet justice, unsweetened.

chapters.title: Ivo's Sister's River
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo finds his sister's final entry: she stayed willingly, and left him the map as goodbye, not summons. He and Ulyana part at the confluence — or almost part. Emotional beat: mourning resolved into gratitude; two runners choosing a shared heading.

chapters.title: Stopping
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. On the riverbank, Ulyana burns her old papers and signs on as the basin's guide for the recovery expeditions — staying where once she only passed through. The village puts her name on their chart. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging, at last, costing less than survival.
